solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Uproarious dances as prisons catch fire in America

indicators.note: the prisons catch, i.e. hold within them, the American firing word

parts.note: cans is slang for prisons or jails
in American slang to can someone is to sack or fire them

explanation.surface: Prisoners riot and dance wildly while flames break out in American jails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like flames in this Bonfire Night puzzle, but it is the American slang for dismissing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a lively, high-kicking French dance, famously boisterous and rowdy.

clue.text: Endless woe and endless tears changed way of ordering things

indicators.note: changed tells us the trimmed letters are rearranged into a new order
endless means the final letter of the exclamation of woe is dropped

parts.note: alack is an old cry of woe or sorrow

indicators.note: endless again strips the last letter, this time from the plural word for weeping drops

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone's misery and weeping eventually shift how they choose things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims ALACK to ALAC and TEARS to TEAR; 'changed' rearranges ALAC plus TEAR (ALACTEAR) into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering from a menu item by item, each dish priced separately, is the restaurant practice described.

clue.text: Free-range landrace that's stuffed with dates

indicators.note: free-range suggests the letters roam loose and settle in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A free-range pig of the Landrace breed has been stuffed with dates for a festive roast.
explanation.walkthrough: Landrace is a breed of pig, so the surface reads as a stuffed joint of pork; 'Free-range' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall chart or almanac is literally filled with the days of the year, so the cryptic phrasing is fair.

clue.text: Saint James we hear comes over as most mischievous

parts.note: James Naughtie is a BBC Radio 4 presenter, the James listeners hear on the Today programme

explanation.surface: A famous radio voice comes across, when heard, as rather badly behaved.
explanation.walkthrough: James Naughtie presented BBC Radio 4's Today programme; 'Saint James' beatifies him by putting ST after his surname. 'we hear' is not a sound signal: it is the voice heard on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of naughty, describing the worst-behaved or most impish of a group.

clue.text: Blazing fire is everywhere

definitions.note: the definition is an adverb for an adjective: rife describes something found all over the place

indicators.note: something blazing is wild and out of control, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A blazing fire has spread to every corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rife is widespread, found all over and in abundance.

clue.text: Reportedly stop American political group

indicators.note: reportedly signals that what we say aloud is spelt differently

parts.note: caulk means to stop up gaps, and US stands for American

explanation.surface: Word has it that someone is halting an American political faction.
explanation.walkthrough: To caulk is to seal or stop up seams; caulk plus US, spoken, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A party meeting or faction of members that chooses candidates or policy, especially in American politics.

clue.text: He sticks out neck to defend male divine burnt at stake

indicators.note: to defend is to surround protectively, so the neck-stretcher wraps round the male letter

parts.note: someone who cranes is a craner, stretching the neck forward to see

explanation.surface: A brave man risks his neck protecting a clergyman who was burnt alive.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Cranmer, Archbishop of Canterbury, was burnt at the stake in Oxford in 1556, one of the Oxford Martyrs.
explanation.definitionFit: A divine is a churchman or theologian; this archbishop was executed by burning under Mary I.

clue.text: Fired dishes' terracotta lining?

indicators.note: a lining sits inside, so the letters are found within the words fired dishes

explanation.surface: A question about the colour inside kiln-fired pottery bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is a brownish-orange clay colour, so it is a shade tending towards red.

clue.text: Fire sleeves insulate end of pipe — it's delicate work

indicators.note: fire sleeves the next word, meaning it wraps round it like a sleeve

parts.note: taken as written
to lag a pipe or tank is to insulate it

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of pipe

explanation.surface: Fireproof sleeves wrapped round the end of a pipe make for fiddly work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleeves' is a verb here: the fire wraps round the insulating word. The answer is a less common variant spelling of filigree.
explanation.definitionFit: Filagree is ornamental openwork of fine wire, a famously intricate craft.

clue.text: Happen to disagree

definitions.meaning: to come about or turn out
friends who ... quarrel and stop speaking

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb has both senses: events can turn out a certain way, and people can quarrel.

clue.text: Used fires to send warning as ocean bed erupts

indicators.note: the seabed erupting sends its letters flying into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Coastal watchers lit warning fires when the sea floor exploded.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilltop signal fires, lit in a chain, once warned of invasion; to light such signals is the verb.

clue.text: Is filled with pitch, a hellish punishment

parts.note: a cup that brims is full to the top
the pitch of a note is its tone

explanation.surface: Something full of tar sounds like a fitting torment in the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch looks like the sticky black tar of hell, but it is musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire and sulphur are the traditional torments of the damned; the old word for sulphur stands for them.

clue.text: Eat round a fire

indicators.note: round means the meal word goes round the letter

parts.note: to lunch is to eat the midday meal

explanation.surface: Someone eating beside a campfire.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire a rocket or missile is to send it off into the air.

clue.text: Clean-limbed Biblical heroine they say is cut in half, then quarters

parts.note: a trim figure is clean-limbed and neat

indicators.note: they say signals that the heroine's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Esther is the Jewish queen of the Old Testament book that bears her name

indicators.note: cut in half keeps only the second half of the little word is

explanation.surface: A shapely Biblical woman is sliced in two, then into four.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests butchery; the definition is 'quarters' in the academic-term sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In some academic calendars terms are called quarters, and a three-month period is a quarter of a year.

clue.text: Kitchen equipment containing English warm ale, brewed in Tyneside

indicators.note: in places the rearranged ale inside the Tyneside letters

parts.note: Tyneside lies in the North East of England, NE

indicators.note: brewed signals the beer words are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A Geordie kitchen holding brewed English ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' turns WARM ALE into AMELWAR, which goes 'in' NE; E for English comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots and pans of steel coated with glossy vitreous glaze are a classic type of cookware.

clue.text: Jet napalming harbour, burning mountain

indicators.note: the two words harbour, or shelter, the answer within them

explanation.surface: A jet aircraft drops napalm on a port, and a mountain burns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbour' looks like a port being bombed, but it is the verb signalling the letters lie within.
explanation.definitionFit: This Sicilian volcano is famously active, spewing fire and lava.

clue.text: They alter resistance, others alter acceleration, time and direction

indicators.note: the second alter tells us to rearrange the word others

parts.note: A is the symbol for acceleration
T is the symbol for time
S for south is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A physics lesson on things that change resistance, speed, time and heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alter' appears twice: the first is in the definition; the second signals OTHERS becomes RHEOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Variable resistors in a circuit, used for dimming lights or controlling motor speed.

clue.text: Pope perhaps is within right to support burning of woman

indicators.note: in a down clue, to support means to sit underneath the preceding piece

parts.note: sati is the former Hindu custom of a widow burning herself on her husband's pyre

indicators.note: within puts the small word inside the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A pope justifies the burning of a woman as his right.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander Pope, the 18th-century poet, wrote biting satire; the surface makes him a pontiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope, author of The Dunciad, is a classic example of a mocking writer.

clue.text: Perhaps a hat which sits on top of mine?

definitions.meaning: a hat is one example of something worn on the head

definitions.text: which sits on top of mine?
definitions.meaning: the winding frame above a pit shaft is called by this name

explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the possessive, but it is a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers both hats and helmets and the winding frame at a colliery pithead.

clue.text: Papers, including Indy, regularly attracting eccentrics

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the name, starting with the first

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing character

explanation.surface: Newspapers, including the Independent, routinely draw odd readers.
explanation.walkthrough: Indy is the nickname of the Independent newspaper, which published this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Identity documents are commonly called one's papers, as in 'show me your papers'.

clue.text: Waif heading off to sit beneath tree, where smoking remains are found

indicators.note: in a down clue the following piece sits below the tree

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the homeless word

parts.note: a stray is a waif, a homeless child or animal

explanation.surface: A homeless child wanders off to sit under a tree, where cigarette ends lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' trims STRAY to TRAY, placed beneath ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish for cigarette ash and stubs, where the leftovers of smoking end up.

clue.text: Fires eliminate central shafts' central part

indicators.note: eliminate means a letter is removed from the shafts

parts.note: axles are the central shafts of wheels
the central letter of the five-letter word for wheel shafts is L

explanation.surface: Fire crews remove the core of a central shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fires' looks like flames in this Bonfire Night puzzle; it means sacks.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the chop is to dismiss them, so both verbs mean sacking.

clue.text: Expanse which is bare, pink and succulent

parts.note: a desert is a barren expanse
rose is a pink colour

explanation.surface: A barren landscape that is somehow pink and juicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succulent' looks like an adjective for juicy; it is the noun, a fleshy plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenium, a fleshy-stemmed plant with pink flowers, is a well-known succulent.

clue.text: Man of leisure died: consumed in the flames he became a martyr

definitions.text: in the flames he became a martyr

indicators.note: consumed means the abbreviation is swallowed inside the man of leisure

parts.note: the phrase 'the life of Riley' describes an easy, carefree existence

explanation.surface: An idle man has died, burnt alive as a martyr.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicholas Ridley, Bishop of London, was burnt at the stake in Oxford in 1555 alongside Latimer.
explanation.definitionFit: This Protestant bishop is one of the Oxford Martyrs, executed by fire under Mary I.

clue.text: Members of northern gentry lie to policeman

parts.note: an animal's lie is its lair or den
DS is a Detective Sergeant, a police rank

explanation.surface: Scottish landowners deceive an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lie' looks like a falsehood, but it is a resting place of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a landed proprietor owning an estate holds this title.

clue.text: Burning of heretic now mostly takes place within metal walls

indicators.note: the trimmed word sits within the two metal symbols forming walls either side

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold, a metal
FE is the chemical symbol for iron, another metal

indicators.note: mostly drops the final letter of the word for now

parts.note: today means now, at the present time

explanation.surface: An execution by fire is staged between metal barriers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal walls' supplies two metals, gold and iron, by their chemical symbols, one on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: This Portuguese phrase, 'act of faith', named the Inquisition's public sentencing and execution by fire.

clue.text: Trick in which fire finally vanishes

indicators.note: finally vanishes says the last letter of the burning word disappears

parts.note: a flame is a fire

explanation.surface: A conjuring act where a fire disappears at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Flam is an old word for a deception, sham or hoax.

clue.text: Bishop killed by fire firstly laid aside battered mitre

indicators.note: firstly takes the opening letter of each of the two following words
battered says the bishop's hat is knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bishop, put to the flames, first set down his crumpled mitre.
explanation.walkthrough: Hugh Latimer, Bishop of Worcester, was burnt with Ridley in Oxford in 1555.
explanation.definitionFit: This Protestant churchman is one of the Oxford Martyrs, executed at the stake by Mary I.

clue.text: Cameron and Osborne's last plan in recession? A sedative.

parts.note: Cameron Diaz is a Hollywood actress

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the chancellor's name
in recession means going backwards, so the plan word is read in reverse

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart

explanation.surface: The 2011 Conservative leaders' last economic plan during a recession needs a calming pill.
explanation.walkthrough: David Cameron and George Osborne were the UK prime minister and chancellor; Cameron is instead the actress Cameron Diaz.
explanation.definitionFit: Valium is the brand name of this widely prescribed tranquilliser for anxiety.

clue.text: Firstly cut the taters (they keep warm)

indicators.note: firstly cut removes the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Chop the potatoes first, an instruction with a cosy aside about warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: Taters is slang for potatoes; dropping the T from 'the' and from 'taters' leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiators, fires and stoves are devices that produce warmth in a room.
